principle: Culture supplies learned norms, expectations and interpretation priors. It never replaces species biology, individual personality, citizenship, organization membership or authoritative world state.
runtime_rules: A character may attach zero, one or many culture_refs.
Culture membership requires upbringing, self-identification, household, education, regional, institutional or other represented provenance.
Species alone never auto-attaches a full culture profile.
A culture profile may contain strong norms while an individual rejects, modifies or selectively follows them.
Cultural knowledge and cultural identity are separate.
Household, kinship, religion, profession, citizenship and organization membership remain separate graphs/state.
Era/date can change cultural institutions and political meanings without rerolling personal identity.
Unknown domains remain unknown and cannot be silently filled with Human defaults.
AI may use a norm only when the character/context has relevant culture state and the norm is visible/known enough for the scene.
AI cannot create marriages, kinship, legal obligations, religious affiliation, titles, Houses, clans or cultural authority for dramatic convenience.

interpretation_policy.strong_norm: May heavily influence expectations/social consequences but still does not force behavior.
interpretation_policy.common_norm: Useful prior that requires contextual confirmation.
interpretation_policy.possible_norm: Can appear but should not be used as default prediction.
interpretation_policy.unknown: Do not generate a canon claim; use individual/project-authored state if needed.

family_policy: Biological reproduction comes from species biology, not culture.
Marriage/partnership, parentage, household, guardianship and inheritance are distinct.
Culture may define social/legal expectations only where sourced or explicitly authored as GAME_ADDITION.
No universal two-parent or pair-bond household model is assumed.
death_policy: Culture may shape funerary or mourning practices only when sourced.
Individual grief remains separate from cultural expectation.
No fixed mourning duration is inferred from a cultural profile unless canon/project data explicitly defines it.
